column1: # The rules' own proof, one case per line: rule, expectation, text.
# "catches" means the rule must match this text, or it would report zero occurrences for data it is
# written to find. "ignores" means it must not, because the text is not personal data: a rule that
# fires on a public handle, a documented placeholder account or a `$HOME`-relative default is noise,
# and noise is how a check like this gets switched off.
# The cases live here rather than in privacy_test.go because they have to contain the shapes they
# detect, and a tracked source file that spells out a home directory is exactly what the ratchet
# forbids — the check did fail on its own test file before this moved.
# Text is the last field, so it may contain tabs only if they are part of the case.
